earlier_scan.source_named: Gusain, Lakhan 2015. Dhundhari (Languages of the World/Materials 435). Muenchen: LINCOM, 88pp grammar sketch (print only; his LWM sketches include phonology)

sources.citation: Bunkar, Suman. 2025. Jaipur jile ki boli ka samajbhashashastriya adhyayan [Sociolinguistic study of the dialect of Jaipur district]. PhD thesis (in Hindi), Dept. of Hindi, University of Rajasthan, Jaipur (guide J. K. Singh). 253 pp. Shodhganga hdl 10603/699868.
sources.note: Ch. 3 (pp. 71-103) sec. 3.5 'khandetar dhvaniyan' has a heading 'balaghat' (pp. 91-92) but it only gives generic textbook definitions of stress (quoting Baburam Saksena and Ramdev Tripathi), the English 'PREsent/preSENT' example and a Hindi sentence-emphasis example; sec. 3.6 says monosyllables carry stress on their sonorous nucleus (generic). No statement of where word stress falls in the Jaipur (Dhundhari) dialect.

sources.citation: Vedamanickam, P. Edward. 2011. Jaipuri. In: Linguistic Survey of India: LSI-Rajasthan, Part I, pp. 367-405. Kolkata: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. [Glottolog 320556]
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number HC437.R3 C34 2014); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number HC437.R3 C34 2014
sources.note: Nothing. 2.1.2 'Supra segmental phonemes' (p. 370): 'Nasalization is the supra segmental phoneme found in Jaipuri language which occurs with all vowels' -- nasalization is the only suprasegmental treated; 2.4 Clusters and 2.5 Syllable contain no stress/accent statement.
Phoneme tables copied from LSI-Rajasthan Jaipuri; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Meena, Sonam. 2020. Acoustic study of vowels in Dhundhari. PhD thesis, School of Language, Literature and Culture Studies, Jawaharlal Nehru University (guide Hari Madhab Ray). Shodhganga hdl 10603/527060.
sources.note: Formant/F0/duration study of Dhundhari vowels (Dausa, Sawai Madhopur, Jaipur). Chapters 1-3 contain only generic remarks that linguistic stress affects F0; no statement about Dhundhari word-stress placement.

sources.citation: Benjamin, Theodor G. & Liahey Ngwazah. 2012. Sociolinguistic survey of selected Rajasthani speech varieties of Rajasthan, India, Vol. 5: Dhundari and Shekhawati. SIL ESR 2012-033.
sources.note: Only other English-language work on Dhundari listed in OLAC; unlikely to state stress but its bibliography may name local (Hindi) descriptive studies of Dhundhari phonology.

sources.citation: Zograf, G. A. 2011. Radzhastkhani jazyk [Rajasthani]. In: T. I. Oranskaia et al. (eds.), Jazyki mira: Novye indoarijskie jazyki, 139-147. Moskva: Academia.
sources.note: Short phonology paragraph (vowel system, phonemic nasalization, Marwari implosives, word tones in NW Marwari); no statement on stress, nothing Jaipuri-specific on prosody.

sources.citation: Ramkrishan. 1977. Hindi aur Rajasthani bhasha ka tulnatmak adhyayan [Comparative study of Hindi and Rajasthani]. (DLI scan, archive.org;ernet.dli.2015.443776)
sources.note: Dhundhari paragraph is dialect geography only; 'balaghat' occurs only in historical sound-change explanations (Hindi). Nothing on Dhundhari stress placement.

sources.citation: Macalister, George. 1976 [orig. 1898]. Rajasthani vyakaran, bhag 1: Jaipur rajya ki boliyon ke vyakaran. Hindi translation (Satyanarayan Swami) of the grammar part of 'Specimens of the dialects spoken in the State of Jeypore'. Jaipur: Rajasthan Bhasha Prachar Sabha.
sources.note: Preface (Jaipur, 24 Feb 1898) says only that the Jaipur-state dialects differ from one another in 'pronunciation of words, grammatical forms, vocabulary and accent (svaraghat)'; the grammar proper begins with noun paradigms; no phonology and no stress-placement statement.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) 1908. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX, Part II: Rajasthani and Gujarati. Calcutta. (Central-Eastern Rajasthani / Jaipuri, pp. 31 ff.)
sources.note: Jaipuri 'Pronunciation' paragraph (a/i interchange, ai for e, loss/transfer of aspiration) says nothing about accent; the only accent remark in the volume is the front-matter note on the acute-accent transcription sign.

sources.citation: Gusain, Lakhan. 2015. Dhundhari. (Languages of the World/Materials 435.) Muenchen: LINCOM. 88 pp. ISBN 9783895867392.

sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PK2215 .G983 2015
sources.note: Only modern linguist-authored description of Dhundhari; publisher blurb says the phonology chapter covers 'suprasegmentals', and Gusain's parallel LINCOM/JNU Bagri grammar (sec. 4.3.2) states an explicit word-stress placement rule, so this is where a Dhundhari stress statement most likely sits.
